name: How to Run a Raid in Foundry

text.content:
The Storyteller runs the raid from The Raid window (the Raid HUD): everyone sees Suspicion, the Limit and the Turn; the Storyteller’s copy has the buttons.

  1. The Entities. In the Actors sidebar, New Entity makes one of the eight with the book’s dice and marked defaults, for the player you pick, and lets the party see each other’s sheets. The same eight are in the compendium The Entities, to drag into the world; then give the player ownership (Configure Ownership). Change the Gift, Perk and Castle Duty on the sheet.
  2. The town. Run one of the three premade towns in this compendium (Chapter 9), or build one with the book’s tables in the Random Tables compendium (Chapter 8).
  3. A new raid. Press New raid and pick the town’s difficulty: Suspicion goes back to 0, the Turn to 1, and the Limit is the difficulty’s. With A new raid resets the Entities on, every Entity is free again and its charges refill.
  4. The shopping list. For a rolled town, Shopping list → Roll the list rolls it; a premade town’s page has a macro that puts its list on the HUD.

• Rolling. Click a trait on the Entity’s sheet. The roll dialog asks for the second die (Mask or Monster) and the Difficulty, offers the Entity’s abilities and help from the others, and has ticks for the situation: Castle Duty, the loud way, watched, the way out of town, the furniture’s extra obstacle and the lock-up. The roll card shows the result, and Suspicion goes on the HUD by itself: one roll, one rise.
  • Costs. On a Cost, the Storyteller picks one on the roll card, and it applies itself.
  • Turns. Press Next Turn at the end of each Turn. After the last Turn comes dawn.
  • Tell checks. When the book calls for a Tell check (Chapter 5), press Tell check, tick who is arriving, name the place, then Roll the check. The system rolls the dice, says whose Tell goes off and raises Suspicion; each place is checked once.
  • Group obstacles. Press Group check before several Entities roll the same group obstacle: their rolls raise Suspicion once, by the biggest trigger among them, and everyone caught flees together.
  • Chases. Trouble at a watched obstacle starts a local chase (by itself, or from the roll card when chases are run by hand), and The Chase tracker opens for everyone: the Lead, the ground, the mob and who still has to roll. Each fleeing Entity rolls from it. Chase on the HUD opens it again.
  • The lock-up. Cornered in a local chase, an Entity is captured and the HUD shows it at the lock-up. From the next Turn its roll is slipping free (tick At the lock-up: slipping free); a rescue that beats the lock-up frees every captive there.
  • The hunt. At the Limit, or at dawn, the whole town hunts, and the final flight runs on the chase tracker.

When the party gets out, the Out of town card gives the Storyteller How the year went (or use End the raid on the HUD). Tick what came home, then Read the year: the card gives the result and the epilogue. A forked party’s year card posts itself.

Running it by hand. Every automation has a switch in Configure Settings → Don't Get Forked: Raise Suspicion automatically, Spend charges automatically, Jekyll becomes Hyde automatically, Apply the Storyteller's Cost, Start the hunt automatically, Show the Raid HUD, Run chases automatically, Run the lock-up automatically, Group checks, Offer how the year went, Carried furniture raises Suspicion each Turn, A new raid resets the Entities, Open the chase tracker when a chase starts.

The compendiums. The Entities: the eight Entities. Random Tables: the book’s random tables. Towns and Guide: this guide and the three towns of Chapter 9, each with its list, location key and map.
